items.title: Français d’origine immigrée traités de « parasites » : Akli Mellouli charge l’extrême droite
items.description: C'est dans un contexte marqué par la montée de l’extrême droite, la hausse des actes antimusulmans et la stigmatisation des Français d’origine immigrée, notamment les Franco-Algériens, que la Grande Mosquée de Paris célèbre son centième anniversaire. Une date qui renvoie directement à la Première Guerre mondiale et à l'implication de milliers de soldats musulmans, venus notamment d'Algérie, du Maroc et de Tunisie, dans la lutte pour la libération de la France. Akli Mellouli rappelle le sacrifie des soldats musulmans pour la France Le sénateur écologiste, Akli Mellouli , a tenu à rappelé cet épisode de l'histoire de France écrit par les combattants algériens, marocains et tunisiens, en réponse à l’extrême droite qui stigmatise les immigrés et les Français issus de l'immigration en les traitant de « parasites sociaux ». Akli Mellouli a aussi profité de la célébration du centenaire de la création de la Grande mosquée de Paris pour rappeler fièrement ses origines algériennes et sa culture musulmane. « Je suis Franco-Algérien et nous sommes de confession musulmane. En tant qu'originaires de ces pays qui ont versé leur sang pour la France, c'est un moment important pour nous de montrer notre présence positive en France », a -t-il déclaré à l’issue d’une rencontre avec le recteur de la Grande mosquée de Paris, Chems-Eddine Hafiz, ce mercredi 7 octobre. Combattants musulmans de la Première Guerre mondiale : « Nous rappelons l'histoire » Le sénateur du Val-de-Marne a souligné que la célébration du centenaire de la Grande mosquée de Paris cette année renvoie directement « au sacrifice des musulmans pendant la guerre de 14-18 ». « En commémorant ce centenaire, nous rappelons l'histoire et nous nous redonnons de la visibilité et de la lisibilité, et nous allons déconstruire le récit de celles et ceux qui nous voient comme des parasites ou des gens qui viennent profiter des aides ou gratter quelque chose », a dénoncé Akli Mellouli. « Les actes islamophobes sont croissants » Le sénateur ne manque pas de revenir sur ce qui se passe actuellement en France, où la parole raciste se libère. « Il y a des femmes qui sont agressées, menacées ou intimidées parce qu'elles portent le voile », a-t-il déploré, assurant que « les actes islamophobes sont croissants » en France. Pour Mellouli, cette situation n'est pas synonyme de fatalité, bien au contraire. Il appelle d'ailleurs à la mobilisation populaire, « quelles que soient les obédiences ou les origines », pour les valeurs de la République et pour la dignité humaine. Le parlementaire explique que la Grande mosquée de Paris « joue déjà un grand rôle » dans cette mobilisation puisqu'elle « fédère et rassemble autour de la question de l'Islam ». À l’issue de son entretien avec le Recteur, le sénateur Akli Mellouli revient sur le centenaire de la Grande Mosquée de Paris et l’hommage qu’elle porte aux soldats musulmans qui ont combattu pour la France. Face à la montée des actes antimusulmans, il appelle à une mobilisation collective pour la dignité humaine et souligne le rôle de la Grande Mosquée de Paris dans le dialogue interreligieux et le rassemblement. — Grande Mosquée de Paris (@mosqueedeparis) October 7, 2026 L’article Français d'origine immigrée traités de « parasites » : Akli Mellouli charge l'extrême droite est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: AFG Bank Guinée et Proparco mobilisent 60 millions d’euros pour soutenir les PME et le commerce
items.description: AFG Bank Guinée et Proparco ont signé, mardi 6 octobre 2026, à la résidence de l’ambassadeur de France en Guinée, au quartier Minière, deux conventions de financement d’un montant global de 60 millions d’euros, destinées à renforcer le financement des petites et moyennes entreprises (PME) et le commerce international en Guinée. L’opération porte sur un prêt senior de 35 millions d’euros en faveur des PME et une enveloppe de garanties Trade Finance de 25 millions d’euros. Selon les responsables de Proparco et de AFG Bank Guinée, ces financements doivent permettre à la banque d’élargir son accompagnement des entreprises locales, de renforcer ses capacités dans le financement du commerce et de faciliter l’accès de ses clients aux marchés régionaux et internationaux. Le prêt de 35 millions d’euros accompagnera notamment l’ambition de AFG Bank Guinée de doubler son portefeuille de financements aux PME, de 60 à 120 millions d’euros d’ici 2027, et de tripler le nombre de PME clientes. La banque prévoit également de relancer sa « Maison de la PME » afin de proposer une offre renforcée et un accompagnement adapté aux entrepreneurs. Les secteurs liés à l’écosystème de Simandou, notamment le transport, l’agriculture, les services, l’industrie, l’énergie et l’alimentation, figurent parmi les domaines ciblés. L’enveloppe de 25 millions d’euros en garanties Trade Finance doit, quant à elle, permettre à AFG Bank Guinée de sécuriser davantage les opérations d’importation de ses clients et de développer ses relations avec les banques correspondantes internationales. Ce mécanisme vise à faciliter l’accès des entreprises guinéennes aux équipements, biens et services nécessaires au développement de leurs activités. Prenant la parole lors de la cérémonie, l’ambassadeur de France en Guinée et en Sierra Leone, Luc Briard, a souligné que cette signature illustre le soutien de la France au secteur privé guinéen et à la diversification de l’économie. Il a également mis en avant le rôle des PME dans la dynamique de développement portée notamment par la vision Simandou 2040 et l’importance de renforcer l’accès des entreprises guinéennes aux financements. Pour Sadio Dicko, directeur régional Afrique de l’Ouest de Proparco, cette opération marque une nouvelle étape dans la relation entre Proparco et le secteur bancaire guinéen. Il a rappelé le partenariat historique avec l’ancienne Société Générale Guinée et estimé que les deux instruments signés offrent désormais à AFG Bank Guinée une capacité d’accompagnement plus large des entrepreneurs, aussi bien pour leurs investissements que pour leurs échanges avec l’extérieur. De son côté, Karim Koné, directeur général de AFG Holding, a indiqué que cette convention traduit l’engagement du groupe à renforcer le financement de l’économie réelle. Il a annoncé l’objectif de porter à 120 millions d’euros les financements accordés aux PME d’ici 2027 et de tripler le nombre d’entreprises accompagnées. Il a également insisté sur l’accompagnement non financier à travers le conseil, la formation et la structuration des projets. L’opération s’inscrit dans l’initiative Choose Africa du groupe Agence française de développement, dédiée au soutien des start-up, TPE et PME africaines. Elle devrait contribuer au maintien et à la création de près de 4 000 emplois directs et indirects en Guinée. Un volet environnemental et social est également prévu afin de renforcer les pratiques ESG de AFG Bank Guinée et de les rapprocher des standards internationaux. Représentant le ministère de l’Industrie et du Commerce, Abdoulaye Diallo, chef de cabinet, a salué une opération qui, selon lui, témoigne de la confiance entre la Guinée, la France et leurs partenaires économiques. Il a notamment souligné l’importance des mécanismes de garantie pour améliorer les outils de financement de l’économie nationale et accompagner les entreprises guinéennes dans différents secteurs. A travers cette convention, AFG Bank Guinée s’engage à mobiliser et à utiliser ces ressources de manière rigoureuse et responsable , afin de maximiser leur impact sur le financement des PME et le développement du commerce international. La banque veillera à orienter ces financements vers des projets viables et créateurs de valeur, dans le respect des exigences de gouvernance, de gestion des risques et des standards environnementaux et sociaux applicables.

items.title: ‘All my respect’ – Ronaldo celebrates Messi after Argentina retirement
items.description: Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo has paid tribute to Lionel Messi following the Argentine captain’s final appearance for the national team. Messi ended his international career on Tuesday night after helping Argentina secure a 3-0 friendly victory over Benin at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires. The 39-year-old scored one of Argentina’s goals and provided two assists as he bowed out after more than two decades of representing his country. Messi, regarded as one of football’s greatest-ever players, described the occasion as “the saddest day of my career” as he brought an emotional chapter of his career to a close. Ronaldo, who shared one of football’s most celebrated rivalries with Messi for more than 15 years, reacted to the Argentine’s farewell post on Instagram on Wednesday. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Leo Messi (@leomessi) The Al-Nassr forward wrote: “Leo, so many years defending your country and a story that will live on forever. You have all my respect for everything you’ve achieved with Argentina. A hug.” The message highlights the respect that has developed between the two superstars despite their long-running rivalry, which defined an era of world football during their respective spells at Real Madrid and Barcelona. Messi had announced his decision to retire from international football in late August, following Argentina’s defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. The decision came after a physically and emotionally demanding tournament, which was also overshadowed by the illness and subsequent death of his father, Jorge Messi. Messi leaves international football as Argentina’s record appearance holder, having made 208 appearances and scored 126 goals for the national team. He also guided Argentina to the 2022 World Cup title and helped the country secure Copa América triumphs during his international career. Ronaldo and Messi have continued to acknowledge each other’s achievements in recent years despite their historic rivalry. Ronaldo also expressed his support for Messi following the death of the Argentine’s father earlier this year. Both players are now in the later stages of their careers, with Messi continuing with Inter Miami in Major League Soccer and Ronaldo representing Saudi Pro League side Al-Nassr. Vanguard News The post ‘All my respect’ – Ronaldo celebrates Messi after Argentina retirement appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Aguelhoc : des coupons alimentaires pour 8 000 personnes
items.description: © Internet Le PAM a commencé les distributions au début de septembre. La première phase couvre environ 1 500 ménages déplacés ou accueillant des familles. Près de 8 000 personnes ont bénéficié d’une première distribution de coupons alimentaires à Aguelhoc, dans la région de Kidal. Selon Aline Samu Nkuelo, représentante et directrice du Programme alimentaire mondial au Mali, l’opération a commencé au début du mois de septembre et concerne environ 1 500 ménages. L’assistance cible des personnes déplacées ainsi que les familles qui les accueillent. Les bénéficiaires utilisent leurs coupons pour acheter des produits alimentaires auprès de commerçants locaux, en fonction des besoins de leur foyer. Ces informations ont été données par la responsable du PAM au cours d’un entretien diffusé le 6 octobre par Studio Tamani. La communication publiée ne précise pas la valeur de chaque coupon, la liste des produits admissibles ou le nombre de commerces participant au dispositif. Une évaluation menée auprès des ménages Avant le lancement de l’opération, le PAM, ses partenaires et d’autres agences ont réalisé une évaluation multisectorielle dans la zone. D’après Aline Samu Nkuelo, trois ménages interrogés sur quatre ont déclaré rencontrer de grandes difficultés pour se nourrir convenablement. La même évaluation a relevé que 99 % des ménages interrogés signalaient une forte baisse de leur pouvoir d’achat. Ce pourcentage concerne les personnes couvertes par l’enquête menée à Aguelhoc. Il ne constitue pas une estimation applicable à l’ensemble des ménages maliens. La responsable du PAM explique que les familles d’accueil partagent leurs ressources avec les nouveaux arrivants. L’opération les intègre donc au dispositif au même titre que les ménages déplacés. Les femmes enceintes ou allaitantes et les jeunes enfants font l’objet d’une attention particulière. Le PAM rattache cette priorité aux niveaux de malnutrition observés dans le nord du pays et aux besoins nutritionnels propres à ces groupes. Des achats auprès des commerçants locaux Le coupon diffère d’une distribution directe de céréales ou d’autres denrées. Il permet au ménage de choisir les produits disponibles auprès des commerçants agréés dans la localité. Ce mécanisme suppose que les marchés disposent de stocks suffisants et que les prix restent suivis pendant l’opération. Il nécessite également un contrôle des coupons remis, des transactions réalisées et des remboursements dus aux commerçants. Le montant attribué à chaque ménage constitue une donnée importante pour apprécier la couverture réelle de l’aide. La communication diffusée le 6 octobre indique le nombre de personnes et de foyers bénéficiaires, mais ne fournit pas cette valeur financière. Aline Samu Nkuelo précise que l’intervention a été préparée avec les autorités maliennes, les responsables communautaires, les organisations non gouvernementales partenaires et les autres agences présentes dans la zone. Une aide nationale fortement ciblée À l’échelle nationale, le PAM estime que plus de 1,5 million de personnes ont été confrontées à une insécurité alimentaire aiguë pendant la période de soudure de juin à août 2026. Une évaluation d’urgence réalisée en juin avait conclu que 40 % des ménages interrogés avaient besoin d’une assistance humanitaire, tandis que 4 % déclaraient en avoir reçu au cours des trois mois précédents. Le PAM indique également que ses difficultés de financement l’ont conduit à réduire la durée de certaines aides de six à trois mois en 2026. Selon l’organisation, plus de 200 000 personnes vulnérables ont été retirées des programmes d’assistance à la suite de cette révision des priorités. À Aguelhoc, le PAM prévoit un suivi après les distributions et la collecte d’avis auprès des bénéficiaires. Aline Samu Nkuelo a indiqué qu’une première observation des effets de l’aide demanderait un à deux mois. Le bilan disponible porte sur le démarrage de l’opération. Il établit que près de 8 000 personnes, réparties dans environ 1 500 ménages, ont reçu des coupons utilisables auprès de commerçants locaux. Les résultats nutritionnels et la durée effective de la prise en charge seront documentés par le suivi annoncé par le PAM. Massiré Diop

items.title: 2027: Tinubu’s win gap over opponents will be unbelievable — Bwala
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has expressed confidence that the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate will secure a much wider margin over his opponents in the 2027 presidential election. Bwala made the assertion while speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today, in response to a question on what gave him confidence that Tinubu could win the 2027 election, despite arguments that the President’s 2023 victory was relatively narrow. He said the odds had also been against Tinubu ahead of the 2023 election, arguing that developments at the time did not favour the President. “The confidence I have is this: all of the statistics and results you read out which happened before President Bola Tinubu won the election at that time, there was nobody who did not know that the odds were not in his favour,” Bwala said. “The governing party at that time, it was clear that they were not working for him. In the real sense of the word, there were policies that were reeled out just before the election that were quite damning to him. “There were governors allegedly who were not excited about that because of some thinking here and there.” According to Bwala, the odds were also against Tinubu during the presidential primary of the All Progressives Congress, APC. “The odds were against him, even at the primary level. He could have been rigged out,” he said. Bwala also pointed to the support Tinubu eventually secured from governors, particularly in the North-East. “Do you know how many governors we recovered? A lot of the governors of the North-East,” he said. He then made a categorical prediction about the margin he expects Tinubu to secure in 2027. “Let me tell you and let me say it categorically, and I will be happy to come back, the gap that President Bola Tinubu will give each and every one of these candidates will be so much that you won’t believe it,” Bwala said. He further cited the number of governors now supporting Tinubu, arguing that their positions give them significant influence over the political structures in their respective states. “President Bola Tinubu has got how many governors on his side? How many governors have joined him? The governors are Chief Executive Officers of their respective states; they coordinate the structures of the state and won their election to be governors,” Bwala added. The post 2027: Tinubu’s win gap over opponents will be unbelievable — Bwala appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Vatican envoy to visit Pakistan from Oct 8-10: FO
items.description: Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher, the secretary for relations with states and international organisations of the Holy See, is set to make an official visit to Pakistan from Oct 8 to 10, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Wednesday. In a statement, the FO noted that the Vatican envoy would visit Pakistan at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. The visit, which coincides with the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and the Vatican, would be the first ever visit to the country by a secretary for relations with states and international organisations of the Holy See. “During the visit, Archbishop Gallagher will meet with the deputy prime minister and foreign minister to discuss matters of mutual interest, including interfaith harmony, dialogue and peace, as well as regional and international developments,” the FO said, adding that the visiting archbishop is also expected to meet Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Archbishop Gallagher is also expected to interact with members of the Catholic community while in Pakistan. “The visit marks an important milestone in the longstanding relations between Pakistan and the Holy See and reflects their shared commitment to further strengthening mutual understanding, cooperation and trust, while promoting interfaith harmony and peace,” the FO added.

items.title: 20 corps members: Police confirm rescue, vow to arrest suspects
items.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka The police have confirmed the rescue of the 20 corps members abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha express way in Imo State last week Thursday A statement endorsed by the Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, said the corps members were rescued at Amakohia Ubi, Owerri West Local Government Area of the state, following a coordinated operation with sister security agencies. Iniedu stated that efforts were ongoing to apprehend those responsible for the abduction and bring them to justice. He noted that the victims were currently receiving medical assessment and necessary care. “The Nigeria Police Force, in collaboration with sister security agencies, rescued the 20 prospective NYSC corps members abducted in Imo State on 1st October 2026. “The victims were rescued on 7th October 2026 at Amakohia Ubi Village, Imo State, following sustained search-and-rescue operations. They have since been taken for medical assessment and necessary care. “Efforts are ongoing to apprehend those responsible for the abduction, as the Police and other security agencies sustain coordinated operations towards bringing all culpable persons to justice. “The Nigeria Police Force appreciates members of the public for their cooperation and support and remains committed to the protection of lives and property, prompt response to security threats and continued collaboration with sister security agencies”, the statement read. items.title: Will not allow military operations, KP CM tells march participants in Khyber
items.description: The PTI convoy led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Sohail Afridi reached the Khyber district on Wednesday with the provincial chief executive vowing that he would not allow another military operation in KP. The route plan for the march, being carried out to demand the release of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, has been changing since it began. The PTI earlier planned that the chief minister would lead his convoy to Khairabad — which borders Punjab’s Attock — on Oct 8 and announce the next plan of action. However, according to a statement released by CM Afridi’s office, he told the protesters in Khyber today that the long march would now go all the way to Swabi, where he would announce the next plan of action. But a member of the PTI’s social media team, Omar Farooq, told Dawn that the final destination remained tentative for now. He also confirmed that the march will reach Peshawar on Thursday and spend the night tomorrow in Charsadda. The plan was also shared by the focal person to the chief minister on social media, Yar Muhammad Khan Niazi. PTI MNA Sajid Khan Mohmand told Dawn that the CM would reach Mohmand on Oct 9 and address a gathering at Mian Mandi Bazaar on Oct 10. The march was announced as part of the PTI’s nationwide protest, initially scheduled for Sept 27 but was later postponed to Oct 4. On Oct 4, the march began from Lakki Marwat and Karak, from where the protesters trekked to Kohat on the second day and arrived in Mattani, located on the outskirts of Peshawar, on Tuesday night. While the plan for the trek after Oct 8 is yet to be announced, the PTI previously announced Islamabad as its final destination. The Centre has warned the party against any protest or gatherings in Islamabad. However, the PTI decided to embark on the march after weekend talks with the federal government to bridge their differences failed for multiple reasons , particularly over the counterterrorism policy. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi again challenged the PTI today to go through Swabi, saying, “Let them cross through Swabi and show us”, while speaking on Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath ’. Afridi decries military operations “I will not allow another military operation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; I will resist anti-people policies till I am the chief minister,” Afridi said while addressing PTI supporters in Khyber. Khyber is also home to Tirah, whose residents had agreed to vacate their homes to facilitate a military operation against terrorists in December 2025. In recent months, the displaced families have expressed reservations over the government’s fulfilment of commitments following their displacement, including the provision of financial assistance. The KP government, led by the PTI, has also been opposed to military operations in the province. Now, it also finds itself at odds with the Centre over the latter’s counterterrorism policy — a sticking point that is said to have led to the breakdown of negotiations between the federal government and the opposition in the Centre, including the PTI. Mentioning those talks, the KP chief minister alleged in his address that attempts were made to compel the provincial government to sign up for another military operation, according to a statement issued by his office. “But I will never become a part of this policy,” he asserted. “The people of Tirah were displaced in extreme winter,” he said, and added without naming anyone that “they did not have any realisation of the hardships faced by the people”. CM Afridi claimed that people were happy in tribal areas before military operations, recalling that PTI founder and ex-prime minister Imran Khan had been voicing opposition to those operations since 2004. He also decried what he described as the provision of insufficient funds for erstwhile tribal areas by the Centre, claiming that his government had released Rs21 billion for families affected by military operations. Noting that the KP government was being accused of not cooperating on counter-terrorism, he argued that terrorism was also prevalent in Balochistan, where the provincial government was cooperating with the Centre. He reiterated his allegation that the Centre had not released the funds allocated for the erstwhile tribal areas, including Khyber, after their merger with KP. Additional input from Mohammad Ashfaq and Fauzee Khan

items.title: Prosecution says journalists’ testimony indicates Matsda2sh was ‘Brotherhood media cell,’ EIPR says statement unproven position
items.description: The Public Prosecution issued a statement on Wednesday regarding the investigations into the six Matsda2sh fact-checking platform’s journalists, stating that one of them admitted that all the defendants — as well as others — had joined a media committee affiliated with the Muslim Brotherhood. It said they had been tasked with carrying out “media plans” based on spreading and broadcasting rumors and false news about state institutions, exclusively highlighting the shortcomings of those institutions, disparaging the roles and performance of their officials and overblowing issues related to select groups, as well as fabricating and exaggerating events related to them. From its side, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, whose lawyers are leading the defense counsel representing the journalists, repeated its demands for their release, for the charges against them to be dropped and for the case to be closed. In response to the prosecution’s statement, EIPR said that its media statements published on social media hold no evidentiary value in law and amount only to a summary of the prosecution’s case, none of which has been presented before a court, while none of its claims has been proven. The organization pointed out the prosecution’s failure to address the fact that the six journalists did not appear before the prosecution until five days after their arrest, during which time they were denied contact with their families and lawyers, in violation of the law, despite relatives and lawyers filing 18 complaints with the prosecution during that period. The prosecution’s statement also failed to mention that the order to hold the journalists in custody is issued by investigating authorities under the exceptional provisions of the counterterrorism law, which only permit the measure “when there is a threat of terrorist crimes and when such measure is required to confront that threat,” according to EIPR. Yet the prosecution’s claims, based on the security investigations, accuse the journalists only of publishing rumors or “false” reports, without identifying “the imminent terrorist threat that required depriving the six journalists of their right to appear before a judicial authority within 24 hours of their arrest, during which documented violations were committed against them.” The six journalists appeared before the prosecutions five days after their forced disappearance following their arrest, during which they were held at National Security Agency premises. None were brought before prosecutors until the first of the six was presented to the Supreme State Security Prosecution on Saturday, with the other five interrogated on the following day. The prosecution ordered that one of the six be brought for forensic medical examination, after some of the defendants complained of being subjected to torture and maltreatment at the NSA premises, with lawyers calling for officers responsible for those premises to be investigated. The prosecution stated that the first journalist who was investigated admitted that the defendants received “monthly funding of sums in foreign currencies,” via bank transfers from a company owned by a “fugitive member of the Muslim Brotherhood” in a foreign country. The prosecution also said it found communication groups on a secure messaging app on his phone, connecting him and the other detainees with the “fugitive member,” as well as emails from the latter to them. All but one admitted to regularly receiving sums of money in US dollars, transferred from a foreign country. After the statement’s publication, EIPR director, Hossam Bahgat, told Mada Masr that the prosecution is pointing to the procedural steps Matsda2sh took to regularize as though it were incriminating evidence. Bahgat noted that following the “ Zambia plane crisis ,” the company that owns the platform registered employment contracts for its staff, which were presented to Egyptian banks in order for accounts to be opened through which the journalists would receive their salaries. Authorities previously arrested a former member of the Matsda2sh team in 2023, after the platform published a series of investigations about a private jet carrying cash, counterfeit gold and weapons, that was taken into custody in Zambia with a number of Egyptian nationals on board, some of whom had alleged military and police backgrounds. The platform mentioned the 2023 incident in a statement on Tuesday, saying that it was followed by extensive security scrutiny by the General Intelligence Services and National Security Agency into the nature of the project, its funding and the journalistic, intellectual and political backgrounds of its editorial team. Three of those currently in remand were among those scrutinized at the time, before the journalist who had been arrested in the wake of the incident was later released. They received assurances that they were not at risk at the time. The platform then applied to Egyptian banks to open accounts for its entire editorial team, submitting proof of employment and company contracts so they could receive their salaries legally. EIPR also expressed surprise that the Public Prosecution’s statement effectively transforms “all the steps that prove the legitimacy and legality of the journalistic practice of the six journalists into evidence of their involvement in a conspiracy against the country.” In its statement announcing that it had ordered the journalists be held in remand detention pending further investigations, the prosecution said that none of the defendants had any visible injuries. It said it had referred three of them, who claimed they were subjected to torture and ill treatment, for forensic medical examination, with forensic reports proving that the journalists had no injuries or signs indicating that violence had been used against them. Bahgat said that none of the journalists reported having visible signs of torture on their bodies and that only one had requested a forensic medical examination. He added that, in denying that they had been tortured, the prosecution relied solely on the forensic report without questioning the officers at the various facilities where the journalists had been held, which was one of the requests submitted by their lawyers during the investigation, particularly after the journalists said they had been forced to record videos in which they recited fabricated confessions under threat of harm. EIPR’s statement responding to the Public Prosecution also noted prosecutors’ failure to record their refusal to hear the journalists’ testimonies or question them as victims after they filed torture complaints against the officers who detained them at National Security Agency facilities in various governorates. EIPR also noted that the prosecution ignored the fact that, during questioning, the journalists had mentioned on record that they were unlawfully coerced into making fabricated, false confessions — a tactic to manufacture evidence for use against them later. The prosecution added in its statement that an examination of the social media account of the journalist who admitted to having joined the Muslim Brotherhood showed that he had broadcast posts supporting the terrorist group and calling for the overthrow of the country’s government. When confronted with the posts, he admitted to publishing them, the prosecution stated. It added that the other journalists denied being members of the Muslim Brotherhood, except for one, who said he had previously joined the group but left before working for the platform. The platform’s statement pointed out that the security scrutiny of the journalists in 2023 concluded with the security agencies affirming that there were no concerns linked to the platform and that neither it nor its editors had any ties to the Muslim Brotherhood or to any political movement, domestic or foreign. According to the platform, this was conveyed to them at the time by political, legal, media and syndicate intermediaries, as well as government figures. The platform alsostated that the security agencies were aware in 2023 that its founder was Abdel Rahman Mansour. “Despite the security agencies’ investigation into the matter, no charges were brought against Mansour or any of the editors. On the contrary, through intermediaries, the agencies asked the platform’s founder to return to Egypt, establish a company and obtain an administrative office.” Claims broadcast on several media channels described Mansour as a Muslim Brotherhood fugitive running the page from abroad. The prosecution stated that another of the detained journalists described the page as aiming to “highlight and exaggerate obstacles related to internal domestic affairs, publicize negative aspects across various sectors and highlight officials’ shortcomings in addressing them, ultimately creating a state of public discontent that would drive citizens to take part in demonstrations to overthrow state institutions.” Nonetheless, Mansour noted to Mada Masr that the platform has previously refuted and corrected claims made by Muslim Brotherhood members. Mansour went on to cite an example published by Matsda2sh in September refuting a statement by broadcaster Mohamed Nasser that repeated “a narrative that presenters on channels broadcasting from abroad have routinely circulated over the past years, holding President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi responsible for building the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam.” The platform also previously corrected an inaccurate claim by Nasser that Sisi did not hold an academic degree when he travelled to the United States. EIPR stated that the prosecution neglected to refer to any news item or report published by the fact-checking platform that could be described as false or fabricated, nor did it indicate any incorrect information or data used in any of the platform’s work, noting that this was consistent with the long investigations that the prosecution undertook with the six journalists over the course of the three days, for almost 30 hours each, in which none of them were questioned in relation to any report that could be described as false or fabricated. On the same note, the platform also stated that it had, over the years, fact-checked “hundreds of misleading statements and widespread rumors promoted by channels and platforms affiliated with the Muslim Brotherhood, alongside statements and rumors promoted by state-owned and private media outlets in Egypt, without bias or equivocation. Some journalists working for foreign-based outlets have even attacked us more than once.” The platform stressed that “we have never been a mouthpiece for a regime or a tool of any group. We belong only to this dream of free, impartial journalism that is not subject to instructions or driven by domestic or foreign agendas.” The post Prosecution says journalists’ testimony indicates Matsda2sh was ‘Brotherhood media cell,’ EIPR says statement unproven position first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: Trump Is Considering a Plan to Strike Iran Before the Midterms
items.description: Sign up for our newsletter about national security here . A fter months of on-again, off-again fighting, the United States hasn’t struck Iran in several weeks. The stretch of relative tranquility is coinciding with the final phase of the midterm-election campaign, and the assumption has been that President Trump will want to keep it going through November 3 so as not to remind voters of an unpopular war that is dragging Republican candidates down nationwide. But that may not be what happens. The White House has asked the Pentagon to develop strike options against Iranian targets that could be exercised ahead of the midterms, according to two administration officials. The planning underscores just how much the president wants to reduce gas prices and demonstrate progress in the conflict before the vote, administration officials told us. The size and targets of the potential strikes—and whether the administration will ultimately proceed—are still being debated. The plans are being developed by U.S. Central Command, which is coordinating the war effort, a U.S. official told us. Even the plans’ advocates acknowledge that limited strikes would not, by themselves, bring Iran to the negotiating table, restore safe travel through the Strait of Hormuz, or lower gas prices before Election Day. But those in favor believe that further action after months of uneasy peace could allow Trump to demonstrate strength and potentially declare some sort of victory, giving Republicans much-needed momentum heading into the election. “It would make the president look like he got a win and that gas prices would start going down,” a Republican familiar with the deliberations told us after being granted anonymity to discuss sensitive matters. A limited operation could be followed up by more substantial military action after the midterms, when Trump has suggested that the conflict, which is now in its eighth month, could resume. Any strike campaign would put the roughly 50,000 U.S. troops in the region, as well as Gulf allies, at risk of Iranian retaliation, and further deplete America’s munitions stockpiles . Even some of the president’s most ardent supporters want the U.S. to exit the war in order to halt the rise in inflation. An inconclusive limited strike is likely to have the opposite effect. Crude-oil prices have typically risen when the U.S. has resumed strikes after a pause, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration . “Military action has done nothing to drive down oil prices; in fact, it has done the opposite,” Will Walldorf, an international-affairs professor at Wake Forest University and a senior fellow at the think tank Defense Priorities, told us. “And if this is an attempt to rally the Republican vote, how does that make any sense given how unpopular this war is?” T he president has repeatedly discussed the possibility of resuming strikes after the election, threatening in a speech to the United Nations last month to “annihilate the Islamic Republic” if Iran did not reach a deal. In an interview with Time magazine released earlier this month, the president reiterated that post-election strikes were possible, saying “we’ve been stocking up for the last six months.” Last week, Trump said he believed the U.S. would win the war “right after the election,” though he added, “Maybe before the election.” Republican candidates see the conflict, and the high gas prices it has caused, as a severe drag on their prospects for keeping a majority in the House and Senate. Ken Paxton, the Republican Senate candidate from Texas, has privately complained that the war has hurt his campaign, telling donors last month that rising gas and diesel prices caused by the conflict were “by far our biggest problem,” according to Axios . [ Read: The real reason Trump wants economic sanctions in Iran ] In recent weeks, the Pentagon has presented Trump with a series of options that would restart hostilities after the midterms, and now Centcom is compiling options for pre-midterm strikes. The post-election menu ranges from small strikes to massive attacks, including further blows to Iran’s energy industry. Even though the Trump administration remains bullish on the effectiveness of its economic pressure campaign, officials caution that Iran may wait several more months before entering serious negotiations. Trump has been publicly furious about the war’s persistence and is believed by those close to him to feel privately humiliated by his inability to bring the conflict to a successful conclusion. He has signaled to aides that he would be willing to strike Iran again, though his advisers believe that the right moment would be after the midterms rather than before. The war is deeply unpopular, and Republicans would not welcome the conflict’s return to the headlines, according to GOP strategists, particularly if more American lives are lost. A White House official stressed to us that Trump “has all options available at any time,” adding that “things will go one of two ways; the easy way or the hard way.” The official did not address our questions about the timing of possible strikes. Oil prices surged after the Iran war began, climbing as high as nearly $118 a barrel in the spring. And although they briefly topped $100 a barrel last month, they have been hovering around $100 a barrel. Gas prices dipped slightly earlier this week amid reports of more tanker traffic transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the vital waterway that carried one-fifth of the world’s oil supply before Iran closed it early in the war. The White House and Republicans facing reelection harbor the hope that further incremental drops will signal lower prices ahead, giving the party some relief before the vote. [ Read: Trump is preparing for a long war ] But Iran has been persistent in its attacks. Earlier this week, it targeted a series of ships attempting to transit the strait, prompting some shipowners to reconsider use of the route. White House officials view those recent attacks as a deliberate swipe at the president, according to people familiar with the West Wing’s thinking. The administration has also said it would release oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve in an effort to increase supplies and keep gasoline prices from rising further. Americans are now paying an average of $4.37 a gallon for gas, according to AAA, compared with just below $3 before the U.S. and Israeli strike campaign began February 28. T he latest military deliberations come as the administration pursues two tracks at once: ongoing military and economic pressure, and indirect negotiations. Washington and Tehran continue to communicate through mediators, but significant differences remain over the terms and sequencing of a cease-fire, an end to the U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the strait’s reopening. Iran may already be anticipating renewed U.S. strikes. Earlier this week, the U.S. removed B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in Britain because U.S. intelligence indicated a possible Iranian-linked attack on the base. Iran has denied any involvement. “Iran is watching the calendar and knows the election is coming,” said one adviser who spoke with us. “And they want to stick it to the president.” At the same time, the White House believes that Tehran is at its weakest point since the conflict began, two administration officials told us. The nation’s economy is teetering. Inflation is soaring. And Iran’s leadership seems in disarray. One close Trump adviser told us that the pattern has been that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps appears to be in charge one day, and then somewhat more moderate political officials the next. Overall, the hard-liners seem to have the upper hand, the officials told us, and they have shown little openness to a deal or even to softening their position. Yet some in Trump’s orbit believe that the moment is rapidly approaching when even the hard-liners may be forced to concede. A strike before the midterms could be seen as a not-so-gentle nudge in that direction—but it could also achieve the opposite, and put the war and its consequences front and center just as Americans cast their votes.

items.title: NAF crash: ‘You didn’t say you wouldn’t return from Abuja’ — Bako’s partner
items.description: The partner of Flight Lieutenant I.S. Bako, one of the 25 people killed in Tuesday’s Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State, has mourned the deceased officer in an emotional social media post. Joanna Yakubu, in a TikTok post on Tuesday, recalled her last conversation with Bako, a co-pilot aboard the ill-fated aircraft. Yakubu said Bako had told her he was travelling to Abuja but gave no indication that he would not return. “It actually Abuja you told me you are going to and you didn’t mention you will not come back. You left me,” she wrote. The NAF aircraft, with registration number NAF 931, was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when it crashed into the swamps of Igbokoda, in Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State. According to the Nigerian Air Force, 25 people were on board, comprising five crew members and 20 passengers. No survivor was found. The Director of Public Relations and Information, NAF, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, said search-and-rescue operations were immediately activated following the crash. Ejodame said NAF 931 was conducting a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when the accident occurred, adding that rescue efforts were conducted in coordination with relevant authorities. “No survivors have been found,” he said. The Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, condoled with the families, colleagues and loved ones of the victims. Aneke described the crash as “a deeply painful moment for the Nigerian Air Force and the nation” and assured the bereaved families of the full support of the Service. Those killed The deceased crew members were identified as Squadron Leader MI Aburime, flight captain; Squadron Leader AP Man-Ugwueje, co-pilot; Flight Lieutenant IS Bako, co-pilot; Warrant Officer Abubakar A, aircraft technician; and Corporal Uguru HC, aircraft technician. The passengers were identified as Flight Lieutenant TL Lazarus, Flight Lieutenant M Akinloye, Flying Officer IM Adeshina, Master Warrant Officer Onwuka F, Master Warrant Officer Matini BA, Warrant Officer Nuhu FS, Flight Sergeant James RB, Flight Sergeant Mohammed AI, Sergeant Ani AE, Sergeant Izibenikien SI, Sergeant Alafuka C, Sergeant Mbadugha AN, Lance Corporal Ugwuba FC, Lance Corporal Eledan GE, Mrs Ezeh Nneka, Godstmine Tarabina, Joy Micheal, Sunday Micheal, Ukeme David and Gideon Omotola. The NAF said Aneke had ordered a comprehensive investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the crash. The post NAF crash: ‘You didn’t say you wouldn’t return from Abuja’ — Bako’s partner appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La chercheuse tunisienne Dhekra Mahmoud, lauréate du prix «France 2026 L’Oréal-Unesco»
items.description: L'Ambassadeur de Tunisie, M. Dhia KHALED, a participé, le 7 octobre 2026, à la cérémonie de remise du prestigieux Prix « France 2026 L'Oréal-UNESCO pour les femmes et la science », décerné en partenariat avec l'Académie des sciences. Ce Prix récompense, chaque année, 35 chercheuses de différents pays, ayant un profil fort prometteur, pour l’excellence de leurs travaux et leur contribution remarquable à la recherche scientifique. Les lauréates ont été sélectionnées par une cinquantaine d’académiciennes et d’académiciens. La cérémonie a été marquée par la remise d'un prix à la chercheuse tunisienne Mme Dhekra Mahmoud, ancienne diplômée de l’ENIT et actuellement post-doctorante, au laboratoire CISPA, leader mondial de la cybersecurité, où elle mène un projet de recherche sur la sécurité informatique. L’Ambassade de Tunisie en France félicite chaleureusement Mme Dhekra Mahmoud pour la qualité de son travail de recherche et pour son parcours distingué, qui illustre l'attachement des femmes scientifiques tunisiennes à persévérer sur la voie du savoir et de l'excellence. L’Ambassade félicite également, et à travers elle l’ensemble de la communauté scientifique et universitaire tunisienne en France pour son engagement dans la promotion de la recherche scientifique et de la coopération tuniso-française. items.title: Canada will not allow assisted suicide for those with only mental illness
items.description: Canada will not allow medically assisted suicide for people whose only condition is mental illness, the justice minister said Wednesday, seeking to close debate on one of the country’s most controversial healthcare issues. Canada legalized assisted dying for those at the end of life in 2016. The right was extended to those suffering from serious and incurable illnesses in 2021, even if death was not “reasonably foreseeable.” Initially, Canada was to allow assisted death regardless of condition by 2024, but that date was pushed back three years, with the government saying it wanted to make sure that the already overwhelmed mental health system was ready. Without government action, people exclusively suffering from a mental illness would have had access to assisted suicide in March, when the exclusion was set to expire. But Justice Minister Sean Fraser told reporters on Wednesday that Canada’s Liberal government plans to pass legislation that will prohibit assisted suicide for people whose only underlying medical condition is mental illness. “Canada has made a decision not to move forward with the expansion (of assisted suicide),” Fraser said. “While there is not a perfect consensus on this issue, we believe this is the correct approach.” Fraser’s announcement follows recommendations from an advisory panel which in June urged the government not to expand assisted suicide rights. That panel raised concern about the lack of mental health support in communities across the country, and the risk that suffering patients would choose death because they could not access care. The committee also highlighted debate among mental health experts as to whether mental illness could ever be deemed incurable. A majority of Canadians support the right to assisted suicide, but in recent months some medical professionals have called for a review of the policy, including how patients receive approval to end their lives. items.title: Coopération médiatique entre les partis politiques: le journaliste Aly Diouf plaide pour la confiance et la connaissance mutuelle
items.description: Chef de service adjoint du Service Enquêtes & Reportages au quotidien national « Le Soleil », Aly Diouf a pris part, du 7 au 16 septembre 2026, en Chine, au Séminaire sur la coopération médiatique entre les partis politiques du monde. Dans son exposé, le journaliste sénégalais, grand spécialiste de la Chine, a insisté sur la nécessité de renforcer les échanges entre médias face à la montée de la désinformation, des «fake news» et des «deepfakes». Il a également partagé son regard sur l’expérience chinoise et les pratiques dont les pays africains pourraient s’inspirer. La coopération médiatique peut contribuer à rapprocher les peuples, corriger les perceptions et renforcer la confiance dans un contexte marqué par la circulation massive de l’information. C’est la conviction défendue par Aly Diouf, journaliste au quotidien national « Le Soleil » et chef de service adjoint du Service Enquêtes & Reportages, lors du séminaire sur la coopération médiatique entre les partis politiques du monde organisé du 7 au 16 septembre 2026 en Chine. Prenant la parole au nom de ses collègues, le journaliste sénégalais a d’abord partagé ses impressions sur les différentes étapes du séjour. Pour développer sa réflexion, il est revenu sur le Sénégal, sa longue tradition électorale, son histoire démocratique et les transitions pacifiques qui lui ont longtemps valu d’être cité en exemple. Il a toutefois livré une lecture critique des évolutions récentes, en insistant sur le poids pris par le numérique dans le débat public. « Armées numériques », fausses informations et « deepfakes » peuvent, selon lui, influencer l’opinion, attaquer les institutions ou amplifier les tensions. Une réalité qui, estime-t-il, dépasse le seul cas sénégalais. Connaissance mutuelle Cette évolution impose, selon lui, une réflexion sur la responsabilité des acteurs politiques et médiatiques. « À une époque où le populisme, l’extrémisme et l’obscurantisme progressent, où le volume des données en circulation est extraordinairement important et où les fausses informations sont devenues monnaie courante, il est grand temps de repenser la démocratie et la responsabilité », a-t-il soutenu. C’est dans ce contexte qu’Aly Diouf situe l’importance de la coopération médiatique entre les partis politiques du monde. Les nouveaux canaux de communication permettent de toucher rapidement des millions de personnes, mais ils facilitent aussi la diffusion de contenus trompeurs. Face à cette réalité, les professionnels des médias ont, dit-il, intérêt à renforcer leurs relations et leurs mécanismes de collaboration. « Aucune coopération ne peut prospérer durablement sans confiance et aucune confiance ne peut exister sans connaissance mutuelle », a déclaré le journaliste. Pour lui, les échanges médiatiques et culturels constituent ainsi des leviers pour rapprocher les sociétés et réduire les incompréhensions. Il a, dès lors, préconisé des collaborations entre rédactions, des voyages de presse, des échanges de contenus, des coproductions, des formations, des réseaux de correspondants et l’utilisation des langues locales. Un regard sur la chine Aly Diouf a également partagé son expérience de la Chine, pays où il a déjà séjourné grâce à un programme du ministère chinois des Affaires étrangères. Il a évoqué son passage à l’Université Renmin ainsi que ses visites dans plusieurs provinces, municipalités et régions autonomes. Des déplacements qui lui ont permis, dit-il, de découvrir ce qu’il appelle la «Chine réelle». M. Diouf cite Shenzhen, devenue un important pôle technologique, Shanghai et sa place financière, Yiwu et son immense marché, Chongqing ou encore Guangzhou. Il dit aussi avoir été marqué par les infrastructures, la planification, la discipline, l’innovation, l’éducation et la politique de lutte contre la pauvreté. L’exposant s’est également intéressé au Gaokao (concours national chinois d’entrée à l’université) et aux «Deux Sessions». Sur le plan international, Aly Diouf a évoqué l’Organisation de coopération de Shanghai, les Brics+, les « Nouvelles Routes de la soie » et le Forum sur la coopération sino-africaine (Focac). Il a aussi fait référence à la politique d’exemption de droits de douane annoncée par Beijing en faveur de produits africains. À son avis, la trajectoire chinoise mérite d’être étudiée dans les domaines de la planification, des infrastructures et de l’innovation. Aly Diouf s’est gardé toutefois de présenter le système chinois comme un modèle à reproduire intégralement. « Je ne veux pas véhiculer l’idée que le système politique chinois est le meilleur », a-t-il précisé. Son approche consiste plutôt à identifier les expériences qui ont produit des résultats et à réfléchir à leur adaptation aux réalités nationales. « Il existe ici de bonnes pratiques que nous pouvons réadapter dans nos pays », a-t-il conclu. Daouda DIOUF

items.title: Trump administration proposes $70,000 fee for Nigerian, other foreign students seeking US jobs
items.description: The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has proposed a $70,000 fee for international students seeking to work in the country, in the latest move by the Trump administration to tighten rules around foreign students and immigration. Under the proposed rule, schools would be required to pay the fee for every international student participating in the Optional Practical Training (OPT) programme, which allows eligible foreign students to work in jobs related to their fields of study while in school or after graduation. International students are generally eligible to work for one year after completing their studies through OPT, while graduates in certain science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) fields can receive an additional two years. The proposed fee would be $70,000 for each student’s initial OPT application and $30,000 for each renewal, per report from AP News. The policy could affect Nigerian students and other international students who rely on OPT to gain work experience in the United States after completing their studies. American universities rely heavily on international students, including those from Nigeria and other countries, for tuition revenue. Technology companies and other businesses also recruit international graduates for technical and specialised positions. Fanta Aw, CEO of NAFSA, an association representing international education, said OPT allows international students to gain practical experience while helping employers fill labour shortages, particularly in STEM fields. “Driving away the talents, perspectives, and aspirations of international students will only hurt American innovation, economic growth, workforce development, and global leadership,” Aw said in a written statement. However, DHS said the proposed fee is intended to address what it considers fraud and abuse within the programme. The department described OPT as a “pipeline for cheap foreign labor.” The public will have 60 days to submit comments on the proposal before DHS can decide whether to finalise and implement the rule. The proposal could also face legal challenges from higher education organisations and business groups, potentially delaying its implementation. Trump administration tightens rules for international students The proposed OPT fee is part of a broader effort by the Trump administration to tighten immigration rules and increase scrutiny of international students in the United States. Last year, the administration terminated the legal status of thousands of international students, with some subsequently detained or deported. The administration also finalised a rule this summer that sought to limit international students’ stay in the US to four years unless they received approval from the federal government to remain longer. Higher education leaders criticised the measure, arguing that it would create additional burdens for universities and noting that some degree programmes are designed to last longer than four years. A federal court blocked the rule from taking effect in September. Doug Rand, a former senior adviser at U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services during the Biden administration, predicted that the proposed OPT fee would face legal challenges. He compared it with a $100,000 fee imposed on H-1B work visas, which are widely used by technology companies and universities to recruit skilled workers. Rand argued that high fees were not the solution. “When we educate international students at our universities, and they want to work and apply their talents here after graduating, of course we should embrace them — not use an exorbitant fee as a pretext to send them packing,” Rand said in an email. items.title: CM Afridi slams Governor Kundi for 'unconstitutional' meetings, claims move intended to provoke KP govt
items.description: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Wednesday slammed Governor Faisal Karim Kundi for holding “unconstitutional” meetings, contending that the move was an “attack on democracy”. His remarks came a day after Governor Kundi chaired a meeting with the KP chief secretary and inspector general (IG) on the province’s security situation. Addressing the 60th cabinet meeting in Peshawar, Afridi said that the KP governor, who belonged to the PPP, staged a “drama” yesterday by summoning the meeting and termed the move “unconstitutional”. “The governor convening such a meeting in the presence of a provincial government with a two-thirds majority is unacceptable,” he said. “The provincial assembly, cabinet and government are fully functional and intact,” the PTI leader asserted, terming Kundi’s act an “attack on the Constitution and democracy”. Afridi contended that the purpose of the governor’s “unconstitutional activities” was to “provoke the provincial government and force it to react”. However, he advised PTI workers to stay peaceful and abide by the law and the Constitution. Calling on the province’s chief secretary and IG, the chief minister urged them not to comply with any unconstitutional or illegal order from anyone if he does not order them to do so. He reiterated that KP’s people and administration had made “countless sacrifices” in the fight against terrorism. “If someone pushes you to follow any unconstitutional order, do not follow it. It can damage our province or the country.” He also called on the chief secretary to urge the provincial administration not to indulge in any unconstitutional activity and to take action against those who were accused of corrupt practices. The chief minister then took aim at Kundi’s PPP, blaming ex-president Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, along with General Yahya Khan, for the separation of East Pakistan, now Bangladesh. He accused President Asif Ali Zardari of “intending to make another East Pakistan here“. “We will not allow any conspiracy to break up Pakistan to succeed,” he asserted. “The party that raised the slogan of democracy separated Bangladesh from Pakistan in the past for its personal interests,” he alleged. “Prioritising personal interests over national interests has been the PPP’s practice,” he further claimed. Responding to Afridi, Kundi said on Geo News ’ programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath ’ said he called the meeting in light keeping in view the prevalent terrorism in the province. He then went on accusing the PTI of facilitating and supporting terrorism. The remarks by the CM and the governor come amid heightened tensions between the Centre and the PTI-led opposition, with the latter going ahead with its long march despite warnings from the Centre of action against any such move. Hours-long talks over the weekend between a joint delegation of the government and PPP, and the opposition alliance ended in a deadlock , with both sides blaming the other for the breakdown. Political temperatures have also remained high due to speculations of the Centre imposing governor’s rule in the province, with Kundi and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi discussing the move on Sunday. ‘Policy shift is necessary’ The KP CM also reiterated his objection to the Centre’s counterterrorism policy and defended his government’s efforts in supporting the police in the fight against terrorism. He contended that terrorism had been “imposed on the province again”, asserting that the PTI-led provincial government had always supported the police and the people of KP. Afridi maintained that he had been making efforts to strengthen the police, the Counter-Terrorism Department and Special Branch since he took the oath on Oct 15, 2025. “The KP police have the most modern weapons and equipment compared with any other police force in Pakistan,” the chief minister said. He contended that the federal government had always treated KP like a “stepchild”. “The tribal districts were merged into KP in 2018, but they have not been fully integrated financially to this day,” CM Afridi claimed, adding that the financial rights of the tribal districts agreed upon at the time of their merger had not been provided yet. The PTI leader went on to claim that federal governments had “continuously imposed military operations” on KP since 2004. “People displaced by the federal government’s wrong policies kept crying on the streets, but they have still not received full compensation,” he said, adding that nearly Rs100 billion in compensation were still outstanding. “Those whose homes were destroyed, families affected and mosques demolished are still wandering from pillar to post for their compensation.” He highlighted that while a compensation of only Rs400,000 per household had been fixed for tribal families, they had not even been paid the promised amount. Afridi stressed that a commitment was also made to provide between Rs370million and Rs380m per month to displaced people from North Waziristan at the Baka Khel camp . “The displaced people of Baka Khel are still not being provided the monthly amount as promised.” “It is the provincial government’s responsibility to stand with people displaced by the federal government’s wrong policies,” the chief minister stated, adding that his government had provided Rs21bn for displaced people. “The provincial government also has to bear responsibility for losses caused by military operations and collateral damage as a result of drone attacks,” Afridi said. He also remarked that the individuals making decisions in the federal government had no sense of the difficulties faced by the people as a result of those decisions. “If the federal government is sincere with KP, it should upgrade the province’s NFC ( National Finance Commission ) share and pay its outstanding dues of around Rs125bn to the province that has sacrificed 80,000 precious lives,” he demanded. Afridi reaffirmed that KP had to fight terrorism as well as deal with the situation created by the federal government’s policies. “The KP government and police are serious about maintaining law and order. Turning the police into personal servants and assigning them other tasks is wrong,” he declared. “If the policy of KP’s stakeholders is followed, peace can be established within 100 days,” the PTI leader insisted. He questioned why peace could not be established in the province “despite 14,000 intelligence-based operations and 22 major military operations over 22 years”, terming it a “failure of the federal policy”. Afridi maintained that if the issue of peace still exists in KP even after 22 years, the federal government should change its policy against terrorism if it was “serious in doing so”. “The excuse that KP is not cooperating is unacceptable; the same policy is also failing in Balochistan,” he claimed, as both provinces have witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years. “The Balochistan government is cooperating with the federal government, but peace has still not been established there,” Afridi said, claiming the Centre’s counterterrorism policy was neither effective in KP nor in Balochistan. “A shift in policy is necessary. KP can establish peace within 100 days,” he reaffirmed. In his address, Afridi also once again criticised Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s remarks that her province faced no threats from India, despite the state’s narrative of the presence of Indian proxies in Pakistan in the face of Fitna al Hindustan. Asif says ‘enough is enough’ Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif assailed the PTI-led KP government for continuing its “complete detachment from terrorism in the province and criminal indifference”. “Enough is enough!!!” he wrote in a post on X. “The PTI provincial government is roaming the streets for a so-called failed political long march, while its facilitators have unleashed a fresh wave of terrorism against the people of KP during this very time,” he said. The minister recalled Tuesday’s attacks in Dera Ismail Khan , where customs officials were among five people killed. He remarked that the entire provincial cabinet, including the chief minister, was “numb to this serious matter and fully engrossed in their politically failed long march”. “As always, these insensitive and shameless people did not even condemn the innocent murder of these five individuals in DI Khan, offered no condolences to the grieving families, did not attend their funerals or, at the very least, visit their homes to express regret,” Asif regretted. “This is inexcusable by any standard.” Instead, the defence minister noted, the KP CM had scheduled a meeting today at his party’s behest to reprimand the IG and chief secretary for attending the governor’s security meeting. “The chief minister and his cabinet of a province under the scourge of terrorism have completely abandoned the province’s people to the mercy of the terrorists. That is why the people of KP are protesting against the provincial government on the streets in various areas. “This can no longer be tolerated,” Asif declared. The defence minister accused the KP government of being in “complete collusion” with terrorists, saying there was evidence available of “its facilitator ecosystem, which every Pakistani has witnessed with their own eyes over the past three years”. Recalling past arrests of ex-premier Nawaz Sharif and his family members, as well as PML-N leaders, Asif asserted: “Time has proven that the allegations were just allegations and they were imprisoned on Imran Khan’s behest.” Yet, he stressed, the PML-N fulfilled its parliamentary role responsibly under the Constitution and did not hold the country and institutions “hostage”. “It fought a legal and constitutional battle in the courts and parliament. It did not ally with the Taliban,” Asif declared. The defence minister said that the “time has come to make crucial decisions”. “KP cannot be left any longer to the mercy of incompetent, insensitive rulers and Taliban allies,” he avowed. Asif further stressed that the unity of the country cannot be put at risk. “An entire province cannot be held hostage. Enough is enough.”

items.title: Syria weighs military aid for Saudi Arabia amid Yemen war, sources say
items.description: By Timour Azhari RIYADH, Oct 7 (Reuters) - Syria is carefully considering providing military assistance to key ally Saudi Arabia amid an escalating war against the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, a US official and a Syrian military official briefed on the matter said. Options being considered include defensive aid to protect the kingdom from attacks, or deployment of forces in an offensive capacity to help Saudi-backed Yemeni troops fight the Houthis, the sources said. The US official said Saudi Arabia had requested that Syria deploy forces to fight the Houthis.

items.title: Fondements du socialisme aux caractéristiques chinoises: une « Nouvelle ère » de réduction des déséquilibres sociaux et de modernisation
items.description: À l’invitation du Département chargé des communications internationales du Parti communiste chinois (Idcpc), des journalistes et responsables politiques d’une trentaine de pays ont séjourné en Chine du 8 au 16 septembre 2026. Un séjour qui leur a permis de découvrir les fondements du « Socialisme aux caractéristiques chinoises » et ses résultats dans la lutte contre la pauvreté. Le Département chargé des communications internationales du Parti communiste chinois (Idcpc) a organisé, du 8 au 16 septembre 2026, un séminaire en Chine à l’intention des journalistes et des membres de partis communistes d’une trentaine de pays, répartis sur les quatre coins du monde. Une occasion pour les hôtes de s’habituer au socialisme aux caractéristiques chinoises prôné par le président Xi Jinping. C’est un président qui a dédié sa vie au développement de son pays. Le 24 octobre 2017, la pensée du président de la République populaire de Chine, Xi Jinping, a été inscrite dans la charte du Parti communiste chinois (Pcc), au côté de la pensée de Mao Zedong et de la théorie de Deng Xiaoping puis en 2018 dans la Constitution de la République populaire de Chine. Tout comme les responsables du Pcc dans les provinces de Shaanxi et de Zhejiang, Madame Sun Haiyan, vice-ministre chargée de l’Idcpc, est revenue largement sur le socialisme aux caractéristiques chinoises. Une adaptation du marxisme-léninisme aux réalités et aux spécificités de la Chine, se distinguant du modèle capitaliste occidental tout en intégrant certains mécanismes de marché et en s’appuyant sur l’ouverture économique. Sous le président Xi Jinping, explique-t-elle, la Chine est entrée dans une « Nouvelle Ère », marquée par une évolution des priorités. Au-delà de la recherche d’une croissance rapide, l’accent est désormais mis sur un développement plus qualitatif, la réduction des déséquilibres sociaux et la modernisation du pays. « Cette vision est notamment associée au ‘’Rêve chinois’’, qui vise le grand renouveau de la nation chinoise et la construction d’une société socialiste forte et moderne », soutient-elle. Cette politique du président Xi Jinping a permis de sortir plus de 800 millions de personnes de l’extrême pauvreté. La visite au village de Nangou dans la province du Shaanxi a permis de mesurer l’effort fait par la Chine dans la lutte contre la pauvreté. Un village qui se trouve dans le plateau du Lœss, un site marqué à la fois par l’érosion et l’accès à l’eau. Les populations qui ne comptaient que sur l’agriculture et l’élevage voyaient leurs conditions de vie se détériorer. En 1998, des mesures ont été prises pour interdire le pâturage sur certaines collines et restaurer les terres dégradées. Lors d’une visite du Président Xi à Nangou, un village qu’il a visité, à plusieurs reprises, il décida de l’introduction de la culture de pommiers à Nangou, dans la mesure où les conditions géoclimatiques étaient favorables à cette culture. C’est ainsi que des techniciens furent envoyés à Nangou pour encadrer les habitants pour s’approprier cette nouvelle culture. Des retenues d’eau furent créées, et à l’aide de pompes et du système de goutte-à-goutte. Les pommiers s’adaptent. Ils donnent de gros fruits juteux commercialisés maintenant dans les quatre coins du monde. Les populations s’organisent en coopératives et disposent de magasins de stockage. Les conditions de vie changent et le revenu moyen par habitant de ce village de 1.000 âmes monte en flèche, se situant actuellement à 31.000 Rmb, soit 250.000 FCfa. Une prouesse. Le chef de la délégation, le Pdg de la Radiotélévision de Trinidad et Tobago, Michael Kerr, qui a salué les efforts de la Chine dans le cadre de la lutte contre la pauvreté, a mis l’accent sur l’importance des échanges entre le Pcc et l’Idcpc et les partis politiques à travers le monde. Il magnifie les efforts visant à approfondir ces échanges et à renforcer la coopération entre les différentes formations politiques autour de ce qu’il présente comme une cause commune et juste. Pour Michael Kerr, le rapprochement des idées et des intérêts constitue ainsi un élément central dans l’évolution des relations entre partis politiques. Dans son intervention, João Lopes exprime l’intérêt de sa formation politique, le Parti communiste portugais pour l’évolution du socialisme aux caractéristiques chinoises. Il a souligné les réalisations de la Chine sous la direction du Parti communiste chinois et dans le cadre du « socialisme aux caractéristiques chinoises ». Aly DIOUF (de retour de Chine)

items.title: Emergency, governor's rule would 'definitely' be imposed if deemed necessary to 'save' KP: Kundi
items.description: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said on Wednesday that if the prime minister and the president deemed it necessary to impose an emergency or governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to “save the province” facing terrorism, it would “definitely be enforced”. The governor’s remarks came during Geo News ’ programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath ’, where the possibility of emergency or governor’s rule was discussed. Responding to questions on the subject, Kundi argued that there had been past instances of emergency and governor’s rule being imposed. “In Balochistan, the PPP had to end its government for law and order and impose an emergency,” he remarked. Asked whether an emergency or governor’s rule would be sustainable if imposed, Kundi replied: “The first thing [to decide] is when and whether it is imposed. We can discuss its sustainability in another programme.” This prompted the host to prod Kundi further, saying his remarks indicated that only imposing an emergency or governor’s rule was being considered and its sustainability would addressed later. Kundi said in response, “We have to save the province, we have to establish peace in the province.” The Centre has warned the PTI-led KP government in recent days of sending it packing through an emergency or governor’s rule as the party goes ahead with a protest march to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. Federal ministers have also cited the security situation in KP in this connection, as reiterated by Kundi. Meanwhile, the march remains a major bone of contention between the government and the main opposition party in the Centre, the PTI, with both taking entrenched positions. On Sunday, Interior Mini­ster Mohsin Naqvi also called on Kundi to discuss the political and security situation amid speculations of ‘imminent’ governor’s rule in the province. The meeting was also mentioned in the Geo News programme, with Kundi being asked whether preparations were under way for an emergency or governor’s rule. But Kundi said the PTI’s long march and security-related matters were discussed during the meeting. The KP governor then went on the accuse the provincial government of “facilitating terrorism” and not doing enough to curb it.

items.title: Muere Maricarmen, la mujer que encendió la lucha contra los desahucios en España
items.description: Maricarmen Abascal, la mujer que encendió la lucha contra los desahucios en España, ha fallecido este miércoles en el Hospital Gregorio Marañón a los 87 años, según ha confirmado el Sindicato de Inquilinas en un comunicado. El 23 de septiembre fue desahuciada de su casa de Retiro , en la que vivió durante siete décadas. Seis años antes, una empresa compró su piso por un precio irrisorio para la zona precisamente porque ella vivía en él. Con una pensión de 1.400 euros, la mujer nunca dejó de pagar el alquiler, de renta antigua, y las facturas: unos 500 euros al mes en total. En 2020 los propietarios le dijeron que debía dejar el apartamento, porque el contrato ya había sido subrogado dos veces, primero a su madre ―que no constaba como inquilina, por una ley franquista― y luego a ella. Y desde entonces la intentaron desalojar cuatro veces y no aceptaron ninguna de las propuestas que recibieron para o bien pagar la diferencia del alquiler (le pedían 1.600 euros) o comprar el apartamento.
